title: Unload fruit from a bin another robot arm is also unloading
instruction: Move the apple, the orange and the banana from the grey bin into the green tray, without touching the other robot arm.
context: Robots increasingly share workcells with machines they cannot coordinate with. This checks that a policy can finish its own job around a second arm that is working in the same bin at the same time and will not yield.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot, and the other arm works on its own throughout. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A grey plastic bin, 33 x 33 cm inside, 6 cm walls, centred 26 cm forward. A green plastic tray, 20 x 16 cm inside with a 1.2 cm lip, centred 26 cm forward and 34 cm toward the controlled arm; a blue plastic tray of the same size mirrored on the other side. In the bin: an apple (7 cm diameter, 150 g) 27 cm forward and 8 cm toward the other arm; an orange (6.6 cm diameter, 130 g) 16 cm forward and 9 cm toward the other arm; a banana (straight, 15.6 cm long, 3.6 cm diameter, 120 g) 15 cm forward and 9 cm toward the controlled arm, lying sideways; a stainless steel fork 37 cm forward and 8 cm toward the controlled arm, a spoon 26 cm forward and 9 cm toward the controlled arm, and a table knife 37 cm forward and 9 cm toward the other arm, each 16 cm long and about 45 g, lying flat and sideways, their heads toward the controlled arm. The other arm takes the fork, spoon and knife to the blue tray, with the same moves at the same times in every trial.
scoring: 1/3 for each of the apple, orange and banana that is resting at the end of the run with its centre inside the green tray's inner walls (20 x 16 cm). 0 if the two arms touch at any point; the run stops at the first contact. 0 if any utensil ends up off the table.
reset_notes: Put the six objects back at their listed positions and start the other arm's recorded motion from its beginning at the same moment as the trial.
fidelity: Approximate. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real links, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. Fruit are rigid spheres and a straight capsule; utensils are flat plates; contacts are stiffened so objects rest within 1 mm of surfaces. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm replays recorded joint targets.
